1-46.name: Entrance Hall
1-46.description: Past the steps and beyond the grand doors, admission to Mount Holly is granted by way of a dark and garish lobby, suitably called the Entrance Hall. From here, each guest's adventure begins; however, the three doors that proceed onward do not always lead to the same adjoining rooms...
notes: Rules for how footsteps work are found on the side table. (Though I think it gets replaced with the trophy list later?)
The letter regarding inheritance is found in this room.
There are two statues in this room. I'll have to update with who of once I find the Foyer.
A painting of Trinsdale Lake is in this room.
There are three bird figures here.
There are two canes here.
There is a coatstand here.

1-46.name: Spare Room
1-46.description: An unfurnished, unfinished and otherwise unremarkable empty room. If there had at some point been plans for this spare room, it would seem those designs are now long forgotten.

1-46.name: Parlor
1-46.description: This cozy lounge furnished with couches and armchairs serves as the perfect social setting for receptions and after parties. Consequently this was one of the most popular rooms for entertaining and the late H. S. Sinclair was known to supply a myriad of parlor games to encourage his guests to think and conversate.
notes: There is a letter from M. Lowry regarding the parlor game, along with instructions for the game in this room.

1-46.name: Closet
1-46.description: A very modest recessed space used for storage. This particular closet is favored by the junior members of the staff, who utilize it to stash away assorted articles and knicknacks whose proper place in the estate is yet unknown to them.
notes: There is an umbrella here.
There is a hat here.

1-46.name: Storeroom
1-46.description: A dedicated storage space filled from end to end with a surplus of chairs, carpets, paintings, and a handful of other things that had at one time been in vogue and on display elsewhere in the house.
notes: There is a building in here.
There is a black vase in here.
There is a globe in here.

1-46.name: Nook
1-46.description: A sung corner reading room which serves as a quiet, private place for guests to spend a few hoursof their afternoon away from the hustle and bustle of the staff.
notes: There is a shelf in the shape of the symbol of either Reddington or Mt. Holly not sure which yet that has colored artifacts on it.
There is a coat stand here.
There is what I believe to be a jukebox here.
There are instructions for taking notes. It includes a lowercase 'beside' which is used as part of a complex clue which leads you to finding one of the missing microchips for the Blackbridge Grotto.

The notes note also has a picture of a journal, which when magnified teaches you how to play the dartboard game and a few other basic clues. I don't have a saved image of the magnified journal though.

1-46.name: Garage
1-46.description: Entering and exiting out through the west facing private drive, the Garage serves as a more practical and informal entrance point into the estate.
notes: You unlock the west path by powering the garage door.
There is a conspicuous box in this room. May be uninteractable though.
There is a note to the driver regarding susipcious absences.

1-46.name: Utility Closet
1-46.description: One benefit of the restoration of old buildings is that it allows the owners to update and add modern amenities. The utility closet and the circuit breaker box within were set up when gas powered lighting was retired and replaced by a more fashionable home electrical system.
notes: You unlock the Gemstone cavern here by inputting the right V.A.C code. Instructions for the code are found in the emails only accessible from the Office.
There is a removed and scratched out switch for 'Cabinet'

Bedrooms.name: Guest Bedroom
Bedrooms.description: A small bedroom maintaned and kept available for accommodating weekend guests and impromptu visitors who find themselves compelled to stay the night.
notes: The room is nautically themed and contains a sailboat, whale, anchor, and ship-wheel.
A letter from 'KL' can be found here regarding the billiard room. Lord Evanson is mentioned in this letter.

Hallways.name: Hallway
Hallways.description: One of the many nondescript hallways snaking through the estate and providing elegant causeways between the more noteworthy destinations that the house has to offer.
notes: There is a conspicuous vase of red flowers on a pedastal
There is a false red note regarding locked rooms here.

Hallways.name: West Wing Hall
Hallways.description: The west wing of the estate has been closed since the death of Lady Epsen. It is unsurprising therefore, that this hallway in its neglected state features boarded windows and dust smothered furniture.
notes: There is a torn note regarding the closing of the West Wing. It has a date on it.
There is a black vase in this room.

Green Rooms.name: Courtyard
Green Rooms.description: A charming spot granting guests a bit of fresh air and open skies within the privacy of the manor walls.

Red Rooms.name: Lavatory
Red Rooms.description: A room one might go to great lengths to avoid showing guests despite them always probing for its location.
notes: You can use the sink to refill the watering can.

Red Rooms.name: Chapel
Red Rooms.description: A private sacristy, as ornate as the most lavish rooms of the estate, is watched over by eight Ajeran Angels depicted in stained glass. This room was more a tribute to your uncle's vanity than it was to his faith.
notes: There are ruby candles here!
There is a missing candle on one of the candelabras here.
There are four statues of unknown figures here.
There are stained glass depictions of all of the Ajrean Angels here. They are used in the Tomb to unlock access to the underground.
The description says eight, but there are only seven angels? I think lighting the torches might reveal the eighth.

Outer Rooms.name: Schoolhouse
Outer Rooms.effect: 📐 Adds 8 Classrooms to today's Draft Pool.
Outer Rooms.description: Long before Reddington Elementary was opened, school convened in a single small building. As the student body grew over the years, the need for separate classrooms for each grade arose and the Mt. Holly Schoolhouse was officially closed down.
notes: There is a desk with 'Herbie' scratched into it.
'within a timely manor' is written on the chalk board.
There is a closing adress written on the desk

The Grounds.name: The Grounds
notes: There is a birdbath near the four flames.

The Grounds.name: Private Drive
notes: There is a birdbath near the gate.
There is a birdbath near the campsite.

The Grounds.name: Apple Orchard
The Grounds.effect: Start each day with an extra 20 👣.
notes: There's a birdbath here.
There's a sundial here.
You can toggle one of the four gas flames here.
The Groundskeeper's Log is found here.
A gemless gem holder is found in the groundskeeper's shed for some reason. ...strange.
The pots here are also broken for some reason.

The Grounds.name: Campsite
The Grounds.effect: You may Call It A Day at anytime.
notes: There's something diggable between the two rocks behind the campsite. ...I dont' remember what clues tell you this though.

The Grounds.name: West Path
notes: There's a birdbath here near the garage.
There's a birdbath here near the Outer Room.
